newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Taylor profit soars, hikes dividend.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Taylor profit soars, hikes dividend.

text.p: British building and property development group Taylor Woodrow Plc reported an 81 percent surge in first half pretax profits on Tuesday to 25.4 million pounds ($39.42 million) and celebrated the progress with a 33 percent rise in the dividend.
The first half payout was raised to one pence, with earnings per share doubling to 4.4 pence on sales of 556.4 million pounds versus 547.4 million.
Chairman Colin Parsons said the overall interim result was "a good wicket to bat on" in the second half, with improvements across all divisions.
Shares bounced higher on the news to a high for the year of 183 pence, but later slipped to 182, up six pence.
Taylor Woodrow reported a rosy start to the second half, which augured well for the full year results.
But the news was hedged with a warning to investors not to automatically expect a rise in the final dividend payout.
"I am inately a cautious individual," said the chairman. "I don't want people counting their chickens before they hatch."
Parsons said the increase in the first half payout was "a little unexpected".

In the results statement itself, the group had explained that the large rise was part of its effort to rebalance payments between the two halves of the year. "This level of increase should not be taken as an indication of the increase, if any, in the final dividend," it said.

Taylor Woodrow also revealed on Tuesday that Tony Palmer, group chief executive, would retire in June 1997 and that a successor was being sought with an appointment expected before the March final results.
The first half results showed "substantial improvements in the profitability of operations in the UK and USA."
But this was partly offset by lower profits from the Canadian and Australian regions.
In the first half, worldwide housebuilding activities saw profits rise to 9.6 million, up five percent.

The property development sector was in line with expectations. Its profits were also 9.6 million in the first half, up 10 percent. But the construction market remained tough, although the division cut back its loss in the first half to 1.2 million from 10.7 million last year.
The British market in particular was reported as very aggressive, with a tougher overseas climate also developing as more domestically-hit firms seeks to spread their wings abroad.
Profits at Greenham Trading rose 12.5 percent to 3.6 million.
